Trading under Publicis Communications Australia
Location: Sydney or Melbourne or Brisbane
 
Account Director (Also known as Business Director)

The purpose of the Account Director role is to manage and take major responsibility and accountability for all aspects of the creative agency’s business in partnership with the client. 
The Account Director manages the workflow, operational and quality processes within the team and across other agency departments, ensuring a high level of effective creative advertising output. The Account Director leads and supports more junior account management team members, maintains a collaborative and productive relationship with strategy, creative & production teams plus establisheds great client relationships at all levels. The Account Director will continually develop a 3-tiered understanding of the client’s business, the industry and the economic influences on the business - Identifying opportunities to grow client business. They will demonstrate Full management of financials – budget control and forecasting, along with meeting growth targets for the accounts through proactive initiatives
Salary: $90k - $105k package


Account Director (Also known as Business Director)

The purpose of the Account Director role is to manage and take major responsibility and accountability for all aspects of the creative agency’s business in partnership with the client. 

The Account Director manages the workflow, operational and quality processes within the team and across other agency departments, ensuring a high level of effective creative advertising output. The Account Director leads and supports more junior account management team members, maintains a collaborative and productive relationship with strategy, creative & production teams plus established great client relationships at all levels. The Account Director will continually develop a 3-tiered understanding of the client’s business, the industry, and the economic influences on the business -Identifying opportunities to grow client business. They will demonstrate Full management of financials –budget control and forecasting, along with meeting growth targets for the accounts through proactive initiatives.

Salary – Over threshold


 
Senior Account Director (Also known as Senior Business Director)

The Senior Account Director is tasked with leading and directing a client portfolio and is accountable for all aspects of the creative agency’s business in relation to their clients.  They develop strong client relationships and lead strategic and creative recommendations across their client portfolio. The role includes the management of a broad agency team and oversight of financial and operational aspects of the account. The Senior Account Director strategically manages the agency-client relationship and is able to independently articulate a clear and actionable strategy that meets objectives. The Senior Account Director seeks out opportunities for generating revenue, developing relationships, winning new business. They will lead new business pitches as requested.  The Senior Account Director has very strong creative evaluation skills and is able to judge when creative is on strategy or not, and is able to work with the creatives to strengthen ideas.  The Senior Account Director possesses a thorough understanding of the production & agency process - Is able to support and explain production estimates and schedules for broadcast/online/print/collateral/etc. and internal agency processes. The Senior Account Director Is able to inspire people at all levels to achieve peak performance, plus career manages and supports direct team by being a mentor and helping them set and achieve their career KPI’s.
Salary – Over threshold

Group Account Director (Also known as Group Business Director)

The Group Account Director is responsible for developing client relationships and leading strategic recommendations across a portfolio of creative advertising accounts. This role is one of leadership and example, inspiring and coaching your team to provide the best possible service to our clients. It plays a senior defining role in developing the Agency’s performance and culture.
The Group Account Director develops and cultivates trusting relationships with client senior management and shows market foresight to effectively anticipate threats and opportunities in your clients’ business. The Group Account Director manages effective communication ideas that drive top line growth and a competitive advantage on clients’ business.  The Group Account Director possesses a thorough understanding of the production & agency process - Is able to support and explain production estimates and schedules for broadcast/online/print/collateral/etc. and internal agency processes. The Group Account Director assumes overall accountability for the management/direction of all activities on your clients. The Group Account Director is responsible for growth and profitability of account portfolio, attaining annual revenue and margin targets, and leads new business efforts working in conjunction with senior management. The Group Account Director is able to inspire people at all levels to achieve peak performance, plus career manages and supports direct team by being a mentor and helping them set and achieve their career KPI’s.

Salary – Over threshold
 
Integrated Lead (also known as Client Partner, Business Director, Group Account Director, Group Business Director)

The Integrated Lead is our key Client Service lead, partnering with our local client team to drive business strategy, creative, content, insights, data and production across a portfolio of our client’s brands. The Integrated Lead will act as a trusted, agency business leader and the client’s business partner, responsible for ensuring that all the right agency capabilities are engaged, at the right time.  The role will lead an Integrated Agency Team, ensuring maximum connectivity, elevating the strategic thinking, driving breakthrough work, and delivering value.  
Role Responsibilities:
·	Lead and partner with our new clients to build rapport and understanding of their business and personal needs
·	Lead and develop complex B2B/HCP healthcare campaigns, across data, strategy, creative and production 
·	Manage teams of individuals from our matrix structure to deliver client requirements on time and on budget
·	Playing a leadership role across our local team of writers, other accounts service, studio, creatives and third parties.
·	Lead and collaborate with the medical writing team and relevant health professionals, to ensure all communications are relevant to the target audience, are of the highest quality and are in line with client briefs.
·	Lead and engage with potential clients, vendors and suppliers (both marketing and medical staff) when required 
·	Overall financial responsibility for all projects

Salary – Over threshold

All of the above roles require a relevant tertiary qualification or a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in lieu of qualification.

Roles could also be available in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication 






 






About Monash Health Pathology Service 






Alfred Health and Monash Health have established a formal partnership to deliver a shared Pathology Service as one of two new pathology networks for metropolitan Melbourne. All roles in the Pathology Programs are working to develop the partnership and ensure we continue to provide high quality care for patients across health services. Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health, it is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state, and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these laboratories is located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings with services being provided to the Public and Private sectors as well as other laboratory services. 












About the Role 






An exciting opportunity exists for enthusiastic and detail-orientated Laboratory Medical Technicians to join the Microbiology department at our Clayton site. We have a number of full-time and part-time fixed-term positions available to support the delivery of high-quality diagnostic microbiology services that contribute to patient care. As part of a collaborative and professional laboratory team, you will play an important role in the processing and analysis of clinical specimens while ensuring compliance with quality, safety and accreditation standards. Our laboratory operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and successful applicants will participate in a rotating roster that includes evening, overnight, weekend and public holiday shifts. 












About You 






To be successful in this role, you will: 









Hold an associate degree or diploma with subjects relevant to pathology or laboratory operations awarded by an Australian TAFE or registered training organisation or recognised equivalent. 









Technical skills- knowledge- experience: 









Experience in the relevant discipline highly regarded 












Good communication skills 












Keyboard and data entry skills 












Knowledge of quality control and assurance procedures 












Familiarity with Pathology LIS 












Able to follow direction from Management. 












Maintain professional standards. 












To be accountable for your technical work 















Why you will love working us us 






Joining our team means becoming part of a dynamic and evolving laboratory service committed to excellence in patient care. You will work alongside experienced and supportive colleagues in an environment that encourages continuous learning, professional development and career growth. 












We also offer a range of attractive benefits, including: 









Ongoing professional development opportunities. 












A collaborative and supportive workplace culture. 












The opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the health and wellbeing of our community every day 












Salary packaging options to maximise your take-home pay. 












Onsite Gym options and ability to join Fitness Passport 












Access to onsite staff parking.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Megan Wieringa or John Hamblin on (03) 9594 4535.


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply

Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

Austmin Development Pty Ltd, is a leader in the dimension stone industry and is seeking a highly motivated, safety-focused, and experienced Mine Deputy to join our dynamic team. This is a pivotal leadership role responsible for ensuring the safe, efficient, and environmentally compliant operation of our granite quarry. If you are a professional with a proven track record in surface mining and a passion for operational excellence, we encourage you to apply.

Key Responsibilities:


Safety & Compliance (Primary Focus):
• Enforce all company safety policies, procedures, and MSHA (Mine Safety and Health Administration) regulations without exception.
• Conduct pre-shift safety inspections of the pit, equipment, and work areas, documenting and correcting hazards promptly.
• Lead safety meetings and training sessions for crew members.
• Investigate all accidents, incidents, and near-misses, and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
• Maintain all required safety and production records in accordance with state and federal laws.

  Operational Excellence:
• Directly supervise quarry personnel and daily mining activities, including drilling, loading, and hauling.
• Oversee the extraction of granite blocks, ensuring quality standards are met.
• Collaborate with the Quarry Manager to develop and execute short-range mining plans.
• Monitor equipment performance and coordinate with maintenance teams to minimise downtime.
• Optimise production processes to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

  Leadership & Team Development:
• Provide direct supervision, guidance, and mentorship to equipment operators and other quarry staff.
• Foster a positive, accountable, and proactive team culture centered on safety and quality.
• Assist in scheduling, assigning tasks, and evaluating crew performance.
 

 Required Qualifications & Certifications:


• A minimum of 5 years of experience in a surface mining environment, with at least 2 years in a supervisory role.
• Strong understanding of quarry operations, including drilling and heavy equipment (e.g., excavators, loaders).
• Excellent problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills.
• Ability to work in a physically demanding outdoor environment in all weather conditions.

What We Offer:


• A competitive salary from $160,000 per annum plus superannuation is commensurate, and a performance-based bonus structure.
• Formal education in Mining Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
• Opportunities for professional development and career advancement within a growing company.
• A company culture that prioritises the well-being of its employees.

Echo Marine Group is an Australian owned and operated company with over 10 years' experience in the Marine Industry. We specialise in the manufacture of Luxury Superyachts and Commercial Workboats. We also carry out maintenance on a full range of vessels in the Superyacht, Workboat and Defence areas.
Due to the increased workload and new upcoming projects, we are looking for enthusiastic and proactive Fitters to join our Engineering Team. So if you are looking for full time employment and have the necessary skills of a Pipe Fitter or Marine Fitter this may be the role for you!
About the Position:
What work will you be doing?
•	Installation of machinery and piping systems into vessels under construction or during maintenance/refit works.
•	Fabrication of piping systems to be installed into vessels, being worked on at Echo Marine.
•	Installation of marine power plants, shafting and auxiliary systems (Note no engine mechanical works is carried out by Echo Marine).
Who are we looking for?
To be successful for this position, you must ideally possess some of the following skills:
•	Marine Fitting experience preferred however, aligned trades including hydraulic piping installation, sprinkler installers or Plumbers will also be considered
•	Be able to read and understand drawings to construct systems and equipment into vessels under construction or maintenance
•	Pipe fabrication including working with stainless and copper nickel.
•	TIG Welding skills, with thin wall tube (1.5mm) experience would be an advantage.
•	Manual tube bending and flaring of tube up to 32mm in diameter.
What we can offer you!!
In return for your skills and experience, Echo Marine Group can offer:
•	Weekly pay
•	4-day 38hr week (Monday – Thursday 5.55am to 3.55pm)
•	Overtime rates apply outside these times and after 38hrs completed)
•	Waterfront location
•	Great small team environment where you are not just a number
•	Interesting and rewarding work
In return for your extensive skills and experience, Echo Marine Group can offer a salary range $39-$45 per hour excluding Super and penalties.
If this sounds like you, please click “APPLY NOW” with your resume and a cover letter.
Only those successfully shortlisted will be contacted.
Echo Marine Group is an equal opportunity employer.

Are you a passionate and experienced chef with a strong background in Asian cuisine? We are looking for a dedicated and skilled Chef to join our busy kitchen team and help deliver authentic, high-quality Asian dishes in a fast-paced hospitality environment.

About the Role
As our Asian Cuisine Chef, you will be responsible for preparing and cooking a range of authentic Asian dishes while maintaining the highest standards of food quality, consistency, and presentation. You will work closely with the kitchen team to ensure efficient service, uphold food safety standards, and contribute to menu development where appropriate.

Prepare and cook authentic Asian cuisine to a consistently high standard.
Ensure all dishes are presented with quality, consistency, and attention to detail.
Maintain a clean, organised, and hygienic kitchen environment.
Work efficiently during busy service periods while supporting the wider kitchen team.
Assist with stock control, ordering, and minimising food waste.
Ensure compliance with all food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety regulations.
Contribute ideas for seasonal specials and menu improvements while maintaining authentic flavours and techniques.
Train and support junior kitchen staff where required.

Requirements
Proven experience as a Chef specialising in Asian cuisine (experience with Chinese, Thai, Indian or other Asian cuisines is highly regarded).

Strong knowledge of traditional Asian cooking techniques, ingredients, and flavour profiles.

Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.

VPT Mechanical Solutions
Kalgoorlie-Boulder, WA 6430
Full-time | Permanent
Salary: $80,000 - $85,000 per annum plus superannuation
 
About the Role
 
VPT Mechanical Solutions is seeking a motivated and reliable Storeperson to join our team in Kalgoorlie-Boulder, Western Australia. This full-time position plays an important role in ensuring the efficient receipt, storage, inventory management, and dispatch of materials and equipment to support our operations.
 
Key Responsibilities

Receive, inspect, and verify incoming goods against delivery documentation, reporting any damage or discrepancies.
Unload deliveries and safely unpack, sort, and store stock in designated warehouse locations.
Use computerised inventory systems to record, monitor, and locate stock items.
Label and organise inventory to ensure efficient storage and retrieval.
Prepare, pack, weigh, and securely package goods for dispatch.
Operate forklifts and other materials handling equipment to move, stack, and retrieve stock safely.
Pick and process customer or workshop orders accurately using manual or electronic picking systems.
Assist with routine stocktakes and maintain accurate inventory records.
Maintain a clean, organised, and safe warehouse in accordance with workplace health and safety procedures.
Support the efficient day-to-day operation of the warehouse by ensuring stock is handled accurately and efficiently.


Skills, Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this position, applicants must meet one of the following:
Hold an AQF Certificate III (or equivalent qualification) in Warehousing Operations, Supply Chain Operations, Logistics, or a related field; or
Have at least three (3) years of full-time relevant work experience as a Storeperson or in a similar warehouse and inventory role.

The successful applicant will also demonstrate:
Experience in warehouse operations, inventory control, and stock management.
Proficiency in using computerised inventory or warehouse management systems.
Ability to safely operate forklifts and other materials handling equipment (a current Forklift Licence is desirable).
Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.
Good communication skills and a commitment to workplace health and safety.
A reliable work ethic and the ability to prioritise tasks in a fast-paced environment.


What We Offer
Full-time permanent employment.
Competitive annual salary of $80,000 - $85,000 plus superannuation.
A supportive and professional team environment.
Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
Long-term employment with an established and growing company.

Cook – Residential Aged Care

Location: Ballarat , Regional Victoria
Employment Type: Full-time
Vacancies: 10
Commencement: Immediate start available for the right applicant
Hours: Minimum 38 hours per week, including weekends, public holidays and shift work as required
Award: Aged Care Award
Pay rate: In accordance with the Aged Care Award 2010, super annuation and applicable penalties
Immediate start available for the right applicant.

About the Role

An exciting opportunity exists for an enthusiastic and reliable Cook to join our Residential Aged Care team. The successful applicant will be responsible for preparing nutritious, high-quality meals that meet the dietary and cultural needs of elderly residents while maintaining exceptional food safety standards.

This is a permanent full-time position offering stable employment and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of older Australians.

Key Responsibilities

•	Prepare, cook and present meals in accordance with approved menus and dietary requirements.
•	Cater for texture-modified diets and special nutritional needs.
•	Maintain a clean and hygienic kitchen in accordance with food safety standards.
•	Monitor stock levels and assist with ordering and stock rotation.
•	Ensure food is stored, handled and prepared safely.
•	Work collaboratively with the care team to support resident wellbeing.
•	Comply with workplace health and safety and infection control procedures.
•	Assist with menu planning and continuous improvement initiatives.

 What We're Looking For

•	Enjoys cooking and takes pride in preparing quality meals.
•	Has good organisational and time management skills.
•	Can work independently and as part of a team.
•	Has a positive attitude and reliable work ethic.
•	Demonstrates excellent communication skills.
•	Is committed to providing quality service to elderly residents.

Highly Regarded: 
•	Certificate III in Commercial Cookery or equivalent qualification.
•	Minimum 1 year experience working as a Cook, Commercial Cook, or Kitchen Cook

Applicants with demonstrated commercial cooking experience, including experience in aged care, healthcare or hospitality environments, are encouraged to apply. 

Training and support may be provided to the right candidate.

Where required by law or the employer's policies, successful applicants may be required to obtain a National Police Check and complete food safety training before commencing employment.

 What We Offer

•	Immediate start available for the right applicant.
•	Full-time permanent employment with a minimum of 38 hours per week.
•	Competitive salary and superannuation.
•	Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
•	Supportive team environment.
•	Opportunity to build skills and progress within the aged care sector.

 How to Apply

Please submit your current resume and a brief cover letter outlining your suitability for the position.
Applications from Australian citizens, permanent residents and all individuals with the legal right to work in Australia are encouraged.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

For any enquiries, please contact Saga Selsby E: saga.selsby@crewesharp.com.au

Position: Motor Mechanic (Automotive Technician)
Company: City Vehicle Services, part of Pickerings Auto Group
Location: Townsville, City Vehicle Services 188 Hugh Street Currajong
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: $78,000 – $88,000 p.a. + Super
Recruitment managed by: Yakr Pty Ltd

About our client:
Our client, City Vehicle Services, is part of the long-established Pickerings Auto Group, a company that has proudly served the automotive needs of Australians for more than 40 years. With a wide portfolio of brands including Ford, GWM, Jeep, Kia, LDV, and Volkswagen, they provide comprehensive vehicle solutions from luxury models to commercial and family vehicles. Based in Townsville, their service centre offers a rewarding career opportunity in a thriving dealership environment, alongside the benefits of a relaxed regional lifestyle.

The role:

Our client is seeking experienced Motor Mechanics to join their growing team. In this role, you will play a critical part in diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining vehicles to ensure safety and optimal performance. You will work with a variety of makes and models while contributing to a professional, team-focused workshop.

Key responsibilities include:
• Conducting inspections and diagnostics to identify and assess mechanical issues.
• Performing repairs and maintenance, including engines, brakes, suspensions, and electrical systems.
• Using diagnostic equipment to troubleshoot complex problems and recommend solutions.
• Following manufacturer guidelines and industry standards to ensure quality outcomes.
• Maintaining detailed service and repair records.
• Staying updated on the latest automotive technologies and practices.
• Communicating clearly with clients regarding repair needs and outcomes.
• Upholding safety standards and maintaining an organised workspace.
• Collaborating with service advisors, technicians, and the parts department to ensure efficient operations.
• Participating in ongoing training and professional development.
• Supporting and mentoring apprentices and junior technicians.
• Assisting manufacturers with specific diagnostic requirements when necessary.

About you:
The ideal candidate will have:
• Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology (or equivalent).
• A minimum of three years’ post-trade experience.
• Strong time management, attention to detail, and problem-solving skills.
• Experience diagnosing faults in engines and electrical systems (preferred but not essential).
• Experience with any of the listed brands (advantageous but not required).
• A proactive and positive approach, with a willingness to take on new challenges.

What’s on offer:
Our client provides a competitive salary, ongoing manufacturer training, and strong management support to help you succeed in your role. At Pickerings, the culture is team-oriented, friendly, and supportive, with a clear focus on the growth and development of their people.
Recruitment for this position is being managed by Yakr Pty Ltd on behalf of our client.
DMLO
